## 7. AI Workflows & Tactics
Date: not provided in source material — [How to Use Claude Cowork – Full Workflow Automation Guide 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SNo_recKZyY)

What it does: Turns Claude from chat into a file-operating workflow agent for repeatable document work.

Tools/models: Claude desktop, `Cowork`, local files.

Setup:
1. Create one working directory with `context`, `projects`, and `output` subfolders.
2. Add `aboutme.md`, `brandvoice.md`, and `workingpreferences.md` to `context`.
3. Set global instructions in Claude desktop/Cowork.
4. Put active source material in `projects`.
5. Ask Cowork to complete the task and save finished artifacts to `output`.

Available now: Presented as available now in Claude desktop/Cowork in the source material.

Why it matters: The core tactic is operational, not prompt-theoretic: constrain the agent to a scoped working directory and persistent context files so outputs become reusable deliverables rather than one-off chat text.

Date: not provided in source material — [How to Use Claude Cowork – Full Workflow Automation Guide 2026](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SNo_recKZyY)

What it does: Converts messy meeting transcripts into client-ready follow-up assets.

Tools/models: Claude desktop, `Cowork`, spreadsheet/document output.

Setup:
1. Place transcript files in the project workspace.
2. Prompt Cowork to extract tasks, owners, deadlines, and priorities.
3. In the same run, ask for one Excel tracker and one sub-150-word follow-up email per client.
4. Direct all outputs to the `output` folder for review/send.

Available now: Presented as available now in the source material.

Why it matters: This is a concrete pattern for collapsing a multi-hour coordination task into a single agent run that produces structured files, not summaries.
